comment: The migration manifest (ADR-0059 Decision 9; docs/design/go-step7.md decisions 3 to 5). Every table and column of the TypeScript server's PostgreSQL schema: where it goes in varlatchd's SQLite schema, or why it is left out; the transformations; what lives outside the database. Rows are written in the canonical encoding (go/server/migration/canonical/CANONICAL.md), columns in the order listed. manifest_test.go holds it to db/testdata/pg-v0.22.0.json, db/mapping.json and schema.sql. A value canonical-v1 refuses (a jsonb number a double does not hold exactly, for one) fails its row, never changes; the export's preflight reports such rows before any barrier.
foreignKeys: The schema's foreign keys form cycles (identities and organization_deletions refer to each other), so no table order satisfies them all: tables are listed by name, the import defers foreign keys and checks every one before it commits.

tables.reason: Better Auth's provider accounts (passwords, OAuth tokens). Varlatch signs people in with passkeys only and never writes a row, so there is nothing to carry; preflight refuses a source where the table is not empty.

tables.note: Copied in event_order, positions kept: PostgreSQL's are 1 to n without gaps, which audit_events_position requires.

tables.reason: PostgreSQL's audit position counter. In SQLite the position is the rowid, checked by audit_events_position, so the copied events carry it.

tables.note: The source's row replaces the one a new database seeds. Preflight requires the backfill finished.

Read in the source's physical order (ctid) and inserted in it: varlatchd reads Requirements in rowid order, as the TypeScript server read PostgreSQL's heap. From the migration on, rowid order is the defined order; PostgreSQL's heap order depended on the planner, so this is an accepted difference.

No session row reaches the target: every live browser session ends, as a sign-out would end it (transformation browser-sessions-end). The rows are exported without their tokens, so varlatchd can end them; the columns map for the reverse migration, which ends varlatchd's sessions the same way.

columns.leftOut: Better Auth's session token, in plaintext (varlatchd keeps its hash): never exported, in either direction.

tables.note: No Go reader: kept so a reverse migration gives the TypeScript server its Convex signer back, and checked as the jwt-signing-key class.

tables.reason: The TypeScript server's applied migrations. The source's are checked against source.migrations; the target records its own schema_version.

Better Auth's short-lived verification values: the challenges of WebAuthn and OAuth ceremonies in flight. They expire within minutes and the barrier refuses new ones, so a ceremony unfinished at the migration fails and is retried against varlatchd. Left out on purpose; preflight reports the row count.

tables.certificate_issuances: The public HTTPS name's certificate issuance count (ADR-0059 Decision 9, step 6 decision 16), schema version 2: varlatchd's own, which the TypeScript server does not keep, so an import writes no row and the count starts empty.
tables.exercise_credentials: What limits an exercise-only credential (ADR-0060), schema version 4: varlatchd's own. An import writes no row, and a reverse carries none: such a credential's own row is copied, and its token_hash ('exercise:' and the hash) matches no token on the TypeScript server.
tables.oidc_token_uses: The tokens exchanged under a binding that takes each once (ADR-0060), schema version 4: varlatchd's own. An import writes no row, and a reverse carries none: the TypeScript server exchanges no token under such a binding (its reserved claim matches none).
tables.one_time_codes_given: The newest time step a seed's code was given for (ADR-0061), schema version 5: varlatchd's own, one row per seed version. An import writes no row, and a reverse carries none. The seeds are value versions and are carried: their env_values rows have deleted_at and current_version_id both set, which the TypeScript server reads as deleted, so it delivers none.
tables.schema_version: Written by the import: the target schema version above.

transformations.text: Every live browser session in the source ends in the target, exactly as a sign-out ends it (migration 0043_session_end_revokes_browser_credentials): its browser credentials become revoked with the same reason, and the same credential.revoked audit events are written. The auth_session_evidence rows CLI hand-off credentials point to are kept, and those credentials stay valid.

The source's audit log is an exact prefix of the target's: the same events in the same positions. After it come only the events browser-sessions-end writes, then one installation.migrated event carrying the source release, the manifest version and the frozen point.

outside.name: convex
outside.reason: The Convex mirror (database convex_self_hosted and the convex-data volume) is non-authoritative and varlatchd has no Convex (ADR-0059 Decision 4). Left out; it stays with the retained old installation.

outside.name: keys
outside.reason: The Root KEK and the BEK are files, not rows: migrate places the same keys in the target's key files.

outside.name: maintenance-and-status-files
outside.reason: maintenance.json and the listener status files in the TypeScript state volume describe that installation's processes, not data.

outside.name: tailnet-node
outside.reason: The tailscale sidecar's node state is not carried: a new tsnet node enrols and takes the name by rename.
